why: Who is a trader: needed to tell a commercial debt from a civil or mixed one (section, proof under commercial-code 30, civil-code 333). Searched the commercial-code text view: only articles 30 and 169 to 202 are in the store.
Acts of trade by their subject (purchase for resale, supply undertakings): needed to say when the debt is commercial. Not in the store.
Acts of trade by their form (companies, bills of exchange): needed to say when a debt between companies is commercial. Not in the store.
Acts of trade by accessory character (a trader's debts for his business): needed for the commercial character of the debt for each party. Not in the store.

Effect of registration in the commercial register on trader status (as remembered; the number is to be checked): the catalogue lists the register extract as a required document and no text in the store grounds it.

Limitation of actions on a bill of exchange (as remembered; the number is to be checked): a commercial debt embodied in a bill or a cheque may have a shorter exchange-law period. The commercial papers chapters are not in the store.

Stay of creditors' individual actions on the judgment opening bankruptcy or judicial settlement (as remembered; the number is to be checked): affects a claim against a trader debtor in a collective procedure. The bankruptcy book is not in the store.
